newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA SHARES SEEN UP NEXT WEEK BUT EYE WEAK RAND.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA SHARES SEEN UP NEXT WEEK BUT EYE WEAK RAND.

text.p: South African shares are expected to remain firm next week on continued hopes for a near-term interest rate reduction, dealers and analysts said on Friday.
But a further slide in the rand, currently plumbing eight-month-lows against the dollar, may unsettle the market's upward swing, they said.

"The rand has weakened out a little bit and we will prefer it to remain steady probably between 4.66 to 4.70 level for the market to maintain it's upward momentum," James Scott, an equity marketing manager at stockbrokers Societe Generale Frankel Pollak told Reuters.

However, other analysts said that although the rand was hitting the local market mood, its weakness should continue to fuel the recent flood of offshore bargain hunters who have sent local stocks soaring to record highs in the past two weeks.
"This market is very strong and we should continue to see it up," Greg Amoils, a portfolio manager at Irish & Menell Rosenberg said.

"I don't know if we are going to see it up 70 or 80 points everyday, but there is some serious foreign buying and we are also looking for an interest rate cut..., a serious one too, not a Mickey Mouse one," he added.
Amoils said foreigners viewed South African shares as much cheaper in international terms as the rand falls.
"When other markets run crazy and we get left behind our PE ratios become far more attractive and the yields in our market start to make more sense.
"This (coming in of foreigners) is pure arbitrage, you sell an expensive market and you buy a cheap one," Amoils said.
One dealer at the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said the market currently looked overbought and was also likely to taper off for some consolidation of recent gains in the coming week.

"I'm still very bullish, but I think the market has been a bit overbought and its got to settle down a little bit. I think the recent big trades we've had have artificially sent us up," the dealer said.

Expectations for an interest rate cut come amid signs that the economy is cooling off and follow indications made by Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals late last month when he said he hoped monetary policy could be eased before end-1997.
General consensus on interest rates among economists is for a reduction in the current quarter, with a total of three cuts expected by June next year.
The only local economic data due out next week which could also give further direction regarding a possible move on interest rates, is the June producer price inflation (PPI).
A Reuters consensus poll of 11 economists forecast the PPI, scheduled for release on Tuesday, would rise 8.3 percent year-on-year or 0.5 month-on-month in June from 8.4 and 0.9 in May.

Among corporate results expected in the coming week are those of metals firm Samancor Ltd, seen battered by falls in metal market prices when it reports on Monday, and De Beers, seen glittering on the back of increased diamond sales when it reports on Tuesday.
